pool.baseline: Sometimes i look at the millions of lights in the skyline and it doesn't feel overwhelming anymore. It just feels... empty. Like, if i were to just stop, the signal would just cut out and the noise of the city would keep playing exactly the same way. It feels like the most honest way to exist is to just accept that i'm not really a part of the music, and just let the static take over.

pool.baseline:
The oil in my lamp is guttering, casting long, twisted shadows against the tent walls that look like the ghosts of the men I lost. The silence here is a physical weight, a crushing pressure on my chest that only the cold steel of my blade seems able to pierce. 

I have nothing left but this shame. I can still hear the rhythm of the drums, the sound of the line breaking—it was my command that broke them. In the old songs, they speak of commanders who find their peace in the finality of the blade, turning their failure into a last, unbreakable oath. They say death is the only way to wash the blood from a soul that has lost its way. 

Is it true? When the shame is this deep, when the debt is written in the lives of better men... is there any dignity left in surviving the disgrace? Or is the only path to true atonement to meet the fallen in the shadows they've cast?
